claims.text: Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Short-step high-temperature annealing followed by controlled cooling and aging can establish a repeatable ductile–brittle–ductile transition in this alloy.
The proposed treatment can avoid the abrupt ductility loss typical of temper-embrittled conventional alloys.
The as-cast alloy contains partially ordered B2 phases.
Partially ordered B2 phases contribute to the alloy's low-temperature brittleness.
Annealing at approximately 1000–1200 °C, quenching, and low-temperature aging will promote well-dispersed B2 precipitates within a BCC matrix.
Controlled ramp rates and dwell times under vacuum or inert atmosphere will produce a refined, uniform precipitate dispersion.
The heat treatment can tailor the fraction and distribution of B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
Tailoring B2 precipitate fraction and distribution alters dislocation slip pathways.
A refined B2 dispersion reduces the risk of forming continuous brittle phases.
Refined B2 precipitates disrupt extensive planar slip or grain-boundary embrittlement in the critical intermediate-temperature window.
Refined B2 precipitates allow dislocations to activate more easily and thereby prevent a steep drop in ductility.
The treated alloy will exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition while retaining sufficient intermediate-temperature ductility.
Conventional steels or Ni-based alloys undergo pronounced temper embrittlement over a narrow temperature range, with a dramatic reduction in ductility.
Overlong annealing or improper quenching may coarsen precipitates and reduce ductility.
The proposed approach primarily applies to BCC-based refractory HEAs capable of forming stable B2 precipitates.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a ductile–brittle–ductile transition, which entails an intervening brittle or low-ductility regime, while also claiming that the treatment avoids an abrupt ductility loss and retains sufficient ductility in that same intermediate-temperature regime. The intended shape and severity of the transition are therefore unclear.

B2 phases are said to contribute to low-temperature brittleness, yet refined B2 precipitates are also said to facilitate dislocation activation and prevent ductility loss. A morphology- or size-dependent distinction is implied but not explicitly defined or supported.
